cabral-erreicht-brasilien#text: Pedro Álvares Cabral was to follow Vasco da Gama's route to India with thirteen ships, but sailed far out to the west into the Atlantic. On 22 April 1500 the fleet sighted land on the coast of today's state of Bahia. Cabral had a cross erected and claimed the territory, which under the Treaty of Tordesillas lay east of the dividing line, for the Portuguese Crown. The scribe Pero Vaz de Caminha described the first encounter with the Tupí in a letter to the king. At first Brazil was used mainly for its red brazilwood, which gave the country its name.
ismail-gruendet-das-safawidenreich#title: Ismail I founds the Safavid Empire
ismail-gruendet-das-safawidenreich#summa: The young leader of a Sufi order captures Tabriz, has himself crowned shah and makes Twelver Shiism the state religion of Persia.
ismail-gruendet-das-safawidenreich#text: The Safavids were originally the heads of a Sufi order in Ardabil whose followers were mainly Turkmen warriors with red caps, the Qizilbash. In 1501 the roughly fourteen-year-old Ismail captured Tabriz and had himself proclaimed shah. Within a few years he subjugated all of Iran and declared the Twelver branch of Shiism the state religion, which he enforced even against the resistance of the Sunni majority. In 1514 he was defeated by the Ottomans at Chaldiran. The Safavids laid the foundations of modern Iran.
michelangelos-david#summary: Michelangelo's marble statue of David, more than five meters high, is set up in Florence.
michelangelos-david#text: Michelangelo Buonarroti created the figure from a block of marble on which other sculptors had previously tried their hand in vain. The statue shows the biblical hero in tense stillness before the fight and became a symbol of the free republic of Florence. It is regarded as a masterpiece of the High Renaissance, which depicted the human body in perfect form after the model of antiquity.
gesetze-von-burgos#title: Montesinos' sermon and the Laws of Burgos
gesetze-von-burgos#summary: After sharp criticism from Dominican friars, the Spanish Crown issues the first regulations to protect Indigenous people in the encomienda.
gesetze-von-burgos#text: On Hispaniola Spanish settlers had been allotted Indigenous people under the encomienda system and forced them to work in gold mines and fields. In Advent 1511 the Dominican Antonio de Montesinos accused the settlers in a sermon of mortal sin and asked whether the Indigenous people were not human beings. In response King Ferdinand issued the Laws of Burgos in December 1512, which regulated working hours, food and religious instruction. They did not call the encomienda itself into question, and in practice they were hardly obeyed.
schlacht-bei-tschaldiran#summary: Selim I defeats the Persian shah Ismail I and secures eastern Anatolia for the Ottomans.
schlacht-bei-tschaldiran#text: The Safavid shah Ismail I had made Shiite Islam the state religion of Persia and found followers among the Turkmen tribes of Anatolia. Sultan Selim I had these followers persecuted and marched against Persia in 1514. On 23 August 1514 he won at Chaldiran in what is now northwestern Iran, above all thanks to his artillery and the Janissaries armed with firearms. Selim briefly occupied Tabriz, and eastern Anatolia came under Ottoman rule. The border between the Sunni Ottoman Empire and Shiite Persia shaped the region for centuries.
erasmus-novum-instrumentum#title: Erasmus publishes the Greek New Testament
erasmus-novum-instrumentum#summary: The first printed edition of the New Testament in Greek, a key work of humanism, appears in Basel.
erasmus-novum-instrumentum#text: For his Novum Instrumentum, Erasmus of Rotterdam compared several manuscripts, set the original Greek text alongside a Latin translation of his own, and added critical notes. In doing so he called into question the Latin Vulgate, authoritative for centuries, and demanded that every Christian should read the Bible for himself. Luther used the second edition of 1519 for his German translation of the New Testament, and Tyndale and Calvin also built on it. Printing made the work available throughout Europe within a few years.
luthers-95-thesen#summary: The Wittenberg theologian Martin Luther criticizes the trade in indulgences in 95 theses and sets off the Reformation.
luthers-95-thesen#text: Luther opposed the idea that one could buy release from the punishment for sins by purchasing letters of indulgence. Thanks to printing, his theses spread across the whole of Germany within a few weeks. In 1521 he refused to recant at the Diet of Worms, was outlawed, and at the Wartburg translated the New Testament into German.
eroberung-aegyptens-durch-selim#summary: With the victory over the Mamluks the Ottomans gain Syria, Egypt and the protectorate over Mecca and Medina.
eroberung-aegyptens-durch-selim#text: In August 1516 Selim I defeated the Mamluk army at Marj Dabiq north of Aleppo; their sultan al-Ghawri was killed. In January 1517 the Ottomans beat the last Mamluk force at Ridaniya outside Cairo and had the Mamluk sultan Tuman Bay executed. The sharif of Mecca submitted, and Selim called himself Servant of the Two Holy Sanctuaries. He took the last Abbasid shadow caliph to Istanbul; later sultans derived their claim to the caliphate from this. The empire became the leading power of the Arab world.
magellans-weltumsegelung#title: The first circumnavigation of the world under Magellan
magellans-weltumsegelung#summary: A Spanish fleet under Ferdinand Magellan sails around the earth for the first time and proves in practice that it is a sphere.
magellans-weltumsegelung#text: In the south of America Magellan found the strait named after him and crossed the Pacific, which he so named because of its calm sea. He himself died in 1521 in the Philippines in a fight with local people. Only one ship, the Victoria under Juan Sebastián Elcano, returned to Spain in 1522 with 18 survivors.
fall-tenochtitlans#summary: Spanish conquistadors under Hernán Cortés capture the capital of the Aztecs.
fall-tenochtitlans#text: Cortés had landed in Mexico in 1519 with a few hundred soldiers and had allied himself with peoples who suffered under Aztec rule. After a siege lasting months, in which smallpox and hunger weakened the defenders, Tenochtitlan fell in August 1521. On the ruins of the city arose Mexico City, the capital of the Spanish viceroyalty of New Spain.
reichstag-zu-worms#title: Diet of Worms: Luther refuses to recant
reichstag-zu-worms#summary: Before Emperor Charles V, Martin Luther refuses to recant his teachings and is thereupon placed under the imperial ban.
reichstag-zu-worms#text: After the pope had excommunicated Luther, the young emperor summoned him to Worms with a guarantee of safe conduct. On 18 April 1521 Luther declared before the emperor and the imperial estates that he could recant only if he were refuted from Holy Scripture, for to act against conscience was neither safe nor wholesome. The Edict of Worms declared him a heretic and banned his writings, but the elector Frederick the Wise had him abducted for appearance's sake and hidden at the Wartburg. There Luther translated the New Testament into German in just eleven weeks.
deutscher-bauernkrieg#summary: Peasants in southern and central Germany rise up against dues and serfdom and are bloodily put down.
deutscher-bauernkrieg#text: Encouraged by the Reformation, the peasants demanded in the Twelve Articles of Memmingen the free election of pastors, the end of serfdom, and lower dues. Luther sharply condemned the revolt and took the side of the princes. The armies of the Swabian League defeated the peasants at Frankenhausen among other places; around 70,000 people lost their lives.
afonsos-briefe-gegen-sklavenhandel#title: Afonso I of Kongo protests against the slave trade
afonsos-briefe-gegen-sklavenhandel#summa: In letters to the king of Portugal, the Christian king of Kongo complains that traders are carrying off free subjects.
afonsos-briefe-gegen-sklavenhandel#text: Afonso I ruled Kongo from 1509 as a committed Christian, had churches and schools built and sent young nobles to Portugal to be educated. At the same time the trade in captives grew, whom Portuguese merchants took to São Tomé and soon to Brazil. In 1526 Afonso wrote to King João III that traders were seizing and selling even free people and members of the nobility, thereby depopulating the country. He demanded that the trade be placed under royal supervision and asked for priests and teachers instead of merchants. His letters are among the earliest African testimonies to the consequences of the Atlantic slave trade.
beginn-transatlantischer-sklavenhandel#t: The beginning of the transatlantic slave trade
beginn-transatlantischer-sklavenhandel#s: For the first time, enslaved Africans are carried off directly from the West African coast to America.
beginn-transatlantischer-sklavenhandel#t: Because the indigenous population of America was dying in great numbers from disease and violence, the colonial rulers looked for labor for plantations and mines. Portuguese and later Spanish, English, French, and Dutch traders bought or seized people on the African coast and carried them across the Atlantic under cruel conditions. By the 19th century more than twelve million people had been carried off in this way.
erste-schlacht-von-panipat#title: First Battle of Panipat: Babur founds the Mughal Empire
erste-schlacht-von-panipat#summary: With field guns and muskets, Babur defeats the far larger army of the Sultan of Delhi and founds the Mughal Empire.
erste-schlacht-von-panipat#text: Babur, a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan, had lost his homeland in the Fergana Valley and launched several advances into India from Kabul. On 21 April 1526 he met the army of Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of Delhi, at Panipat north of Delhi. Babur combined a wagon fortress, field artillery and muskets with flanking attacks by his cavalry and won; Ibrahim was killed. In 1527 he also defeated the Rajput princes. His successors, the Great Mughals, ruled India for more than 300 years.
schlacht-bei-mohacs#summary: Suleiman the Magnificent destroys the Hungarian army; King Louis II is killed, and the Kingdom of Hungary falls apart.
schlacht-bei-mohacs#text: On 29 August 1526 Suleiman's troops met the much smaller army of King Louis II of Hungary and Bohemia at Mohács on the Danube. The Ottoman artillery and the Janissaries decided the battle within a few hours; Louis drowned while fleeing. The Habsburg Ferdinand and the Hungarian nobleman John Zápolya disputed his succession. In 1541 the Ottomans took Buda, and central Hungary became an Ottoman province for 150 years. Hungary remained divided between the Habsburgs, the Ottomans and the Principality of Transylvania.
bruderkrieg-im-inkareich#title: Death of Huayna Capac and the war of the brothers
bruderkrieg-im-inkareich#summary: An epidemic kills the Inca Huayna Capac, and his sons Huáscar and Atahualpa fight for power.
bruderkrieg-im-inkareich#text: Around 1527 Huayna Capac died in the north of the empire of an epidemic, probably smallpox, which spread from the European settlements faster than the Spaniards themselves. His designated successor also died. Thereupon two sons claimed the throne: Huáscar, who was recognized in Cusco, and Atahualpa, who relied on the experienced army in the north. The civil war devastated wide areas. In 1532 Atahualpa's generals captured Huáscar, shortly before Francisco Pizarro and his men arrived in the empire.
krieg-gegen-ahmad-gran#title: Ethiopia at war with Ahmad Gragn
krieg-gegen-ahmad-gran#summary: The imam of the Sultanate of Adal conquers large parts of Christian Ethiopia until he is defeated with Portuguese help.
krieg-gegen-ahmad-gran#text: Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim, called Gragn, the left-handed, by the Ethiopians, led the troops of the Muslim Sultanate of Adal in the east of the Horn of Africa. After his victory at Shimbra Kure in 1529 he overran large parts of the empire with firearms obtained from the Ottoman Empire and destroyed many churches and monasteries. Emperor Lebna Dengel died in 1540 while in flight. His son Galawdewos received support from a small Portuguese force and defeated Ahmad in 1543 at Wayna Daga, where the imam was killed. The war weakened both sides and made it easier for the Oromo to migrate into the highlands.
erste-belagerung-wiens#summary: Suleiman besieges the Habsburg residence of Vienna, but has to withdraw after three weeks.
erste-belagerung-wiens#text: After taking Buda and installing John Zápolya as vassal king, Suleiman advanced up the Danube with a large army in 1529 and encircled Vienna at the end of September. The city was defended by a small garrison under Count Niklas Salm, which repelled several mines and assaults. Long supply lines, rain and the approaching winter forced the Ottomans to withdraw in mid-October. The siege shocked Europe and, in the Holy Roman Empire, intensified the fear of the "Turks" spread by pamphlets and sermons. In the following years the Turkish threat repeatedly obliged Emperor Charles V to make concessions to the Protestants, whose help he needed.
eroberung-des-inkareiches#title: The conquest of the Inca empire
eroberung-des-inkareiches#summary: Francisco Pizarro takes the Inca ruler Atahualpa prisoner and brings the largest empire in South America under Spanish control.
eroberung-des-inkareiches#text: With fewer than 200 men, Pizarro lured the Inca Atahualpa into an ambush at Cajamarca and had his retinue slaughtered. Despite an enormous ransom in gold and silver, Atahualpa was executed in 1533. A preceding civil war and imported epidemics had weakened the empire; in 1535 the Spaniards founded Lima and exploited the silver mines of Potosí.
vizekoenigreich-neuspanien#title: Founding of the Viceroyalty of New Spain
vizekoenigreich-neuspanien#summary: With Antonio de Mendoza the first viceroy takes office in Mexico City; the Crown takes over rule from the conquistadors.
vizekoenigreich-neuspanien#text: After the conquest of the Aztec Empire, Emperor Charles V distrusted the power of the conquistadors and installed a direct representative. In 1535 Antonio de Mendoza arrived in Mexico City as the first viceroy and built up the administration, the tax system and a mint. New Spain eventually stretched from the territory of today's United States through Central America and the Caribbean to the Philippines. In 1542 the Viceroyalty of Peru followed, with its capital Lima. The viceroyalties lasted for almost three centuries until independence.
neue-gesetze-1542#title: The New Laws ban the enslavement of Indigenous people
neue-gesetze-1542#summary: Charles V declares Indigenous people free subjects of the Crown and intends to let the encomienda expire.
neue-gesetze-1542#text: Under the impact of the reports of Bartolomé de Las Casas, Charles V signed the New Laws in November 1542. They banned the enslavement of Indigenous people, prohibited the granting of new encomiendas and decreed that existing ones should revert to the Crown on the death of their holders. In Peru settlers under Gonzalo Pizarro rose up in response and killed the viceroy in 1546. The Crown withdrew the inheritance rule in 1545, yet the encomienda gradually lost importance. The laws are regarded as early evidence of a debate about human rights.
kopernikus-heliozentrisches-weltbild#tit: Copernicus publishes the heliocentric model of the universe
kopernikus-heliozentrisches-weltbild#sum: In his principal work, Nicolaus Copernicus places the sun rather than the earth at the center of the universe.
kopernikus-heliozentrisches-weltbild#tex: The book De revolutionibus orbium coelestium appeared in Nuremberg shortly before the death of its author. Copernicus explained the movements of the planets more simply by having the earth circle the sun, and in doing so he contradicted the teaching of Ptolemy, which had been accepted since antiquity. His model was later confirmed and developed further by Kepler, Galileo, and Newton, and it marks the beginning of modern astronomy.
vesalius-anatomie#summary: With his work De humani corporis fabrica, Andreas Vesalius replaces the ancient teaching of Galen with observations of the dissected human body.
vesalius-anatomie#text: Vesalius, who came from Brussels, taught in Padua and dissected himself instead of watching an assistant and reading aloud from Galen, as was usual. In doing so he found more than 200 errors in ancient anatomy, which Galen had derived from animals. His work in seven books, printed in Basel in 1543, combined precise descriptions with masterly woodcuts from the workshop of Titian. The Fabrica made the human body an object of independent research and became the foundation of scientific medicine.
silberberg-von-potosi#title: Discovery of the silver mountain of Potosí
silberberg-von-potosi#summary: In the highlands of today's Bolivia the Spaniards come upon the Cerro Rico, the richest silver deposit of the early modern period.
silberberg-von-potosi#text: At the foot of the Cerro Rico, at an altitude of more than 4,000 metres, one of the largest cities in the Americas grew up within a few decades. From the 1570s Viceroy Francisco de Toledo obliged Indigenous villages under the mita system to send thousands of men to the mines every year. With the amalgamation process and mercury from Huancavelica, output rose sharply, but many workers died from accidents, cold and poisoning. Silver from Potosí financed Spain's wars and travelled via Europe as far as China. To this day the name Potosí stands for both immeasurable wealth and exploitation.
konzil-von-trient#summary: The Catholic Church responds to the Reformation with a clarification of its teaching and with internal reforms.
konzil-von-trient#text: In three sessions over 18 years, the bishops affirmed the Catholic doctrine of the sacraments, of tradition, and of justification, and marked it off clearly from the Protestant positions. At the same time abuses such as the sale of offices were combated and seminaries were established for better training. The council shaped Catholicism into the 20th century and deepened the division of Christendom.
gruendung-von-salvador-da-bahia#summary: Portugal installs a governor-general in Brazil and founds Salvador as the capital of the colony.
gruendung-von-salvador-da-bahia#text: The system of private captaincies, to which Portugal had granted the Brazilian coast since 1534, had largely failed. In 1549 Tomé de Sousa arrived as the first governor-general in the Bay of All Saints and founded Salvador. With him came the first Jesuits under Manuel da Nóbrega, who began the mission among the Tupí. In the following decades sugar plantations grew in Bahia and Pernambuco, on which more and more enslaved Africans were forced to work. Salvador remained the capital of Brazil until 1763.
ausbau-der-grossen-mauer-unter-den-ming#: Expansion of the Great Wall under the Ming
After Mongol raids reach the gates of Beijing, the Ming turn the frontier fortifications into the wall of stone and brick known today as the Great Wall.

The Ming emperors increasingly relied on defence against the Mongols. After the Mongol ruler Altan Khan had advanced to the outskirts of Beijing in 1550, the northern fortifications were strengthened at great expense. Especially under General Qi Jiguang, sections of brick and stone with closely spaced watchtowers were built from the late 1560s onwards. The Ming wall runs from the Shanhaiguan pass on the sea to Jiayuguan in the west. Most of the sections visited today, such as Badaling, date from this period.
disputation-von-valladolid#summary: Before a commission of scholars, Bartolomé de Las Casas and Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda argue over the legitimacy of the conquest of the Americas.
disputation-von-valladolid#text: Charles V temporarily suspended new campaigns of conquest until theologians and jurists had clarified whether war against the Indigenous peoples was permissible. Sepúlveda appealed to Aristotle and claimed that the Indigenous peoples were by nature destined for subordination. Las Casas countered that they were rational human beings with kingdoms of their own and could be led to the faith only by peaceful means. The commission reached no clear verdict. The debate is nevertheless regarded as one of Europe's first great disputes about the rights of foreign peoples.
bau-der-sueleymaniye-moschee#summary: The court architect Sinan erects for Suleiman, on one of Istanbul's hills, one of the largest mosque complexes in the Islamic world.
bau-der-sueleymaniye-moschee#text: From 1550 to 1557 Sinan built the Süleymaniye Mosque on Suleiman's commission; its dome still dominates the skyline of Istanbul. The complex included madrasas, a medical school, a hospital, a soup kitchen, a caravanserai, a bath and a library. Sinan took the Hagia Sophia as his model but made the interior brighter and more clearly structured. In the garden lie the tombs of Suleiman and his wife Hürrem. The foundation shows how mosques were at the same time social and educational centres.
universitaeten-lima-und-mexiko#title: First universities in Lima and Mexico
universitaeten-lima-und-mexiko#summary: The Spanish Crown founds the first universities on the American mainland in Lima and Mexico City.
universitaeten-lima-und-mexiko#text: In May 1551 the university that survives today as the National University of San Marcos was founded in Lima, and in September a royal decree followed for the University of Mexico. On the model of Salamanca they taught theology, canon law, law, medicine and the arts. In Mexico there were also chairs for Indigenous languages such as Nahuatl, because priests were to be trained for the mission. The universities mainly educated clergy and lawyers from Creole families, who later formed the backbone of the administration.
augsburger-religionsfrieden#summary: The Diet of Augsburg recognizes the Lutheran confession in the empire and leaves the choice of denomination to the territorial rulers.
augsburger-religionsfrieden#text: After the Schmalkaldic War and the revolt of the princes, Charles V had come to see that the Protestants could not be forced back into the old church, and he left the negotiations to his brother Ferdinand. The peace proclaimed on 25 September 1555 granted each imperial estate the right to determine the Catholic or the Lutheran confession for its own territory; subjects of another faith were allowed to emigrate. Later this principle was summed up in the formula that whoever rules the land determines its religion. Calvinists remained excluded, and unresolved disputes contributed to the outbreak of the Thirty Years' War in 1618.
erste-kaffeehaeuser-in-istanbul#summary: Two merchants from Syria open coffeehouses in Istanbul, which quickly become popular meeting places.
erste-kaffeehaeuser-in-istanbul#text: Coffee came from Yemen and in the 15th century was popular among Sufis, who used it to stay awake during nightly devotions. According to the Ottoman chronicler Peçevi, two men from Aleppo and Damascus opened the first coffeehouses around 1555 in Istanbul's Tahtakale quarter. There men met to talk, to play board games and to listen to poets and storytellers. Religious scholars and sultans distrusted these places of criticism; Murad IV had them closed in 1633. In the 17th century coffee reached Europe by way of Venice and Vienna.
akbar-mogulreich#title: Akbar becomes ruler of the Mughal empire
akbar-mogulreich#summary: The thirteen-year-old Akbar ascends the throne and builds the Mughal empire into the dominant power in India with a policy of religious tolerance.
akbar-mogulreich#text: The Mughal empire had been founded by Babur in 1526, but it was Akbar who secured it for good: after his victory at the second battle of Panipat in 1556, he subdued northern India, Gujarat, and Bengal over the following decades. He bound the Hindu Rajputs to himself through marriages and offices, abolished the special tax on non-Muslims in 1564, and had Muslims, Hindus, Jains, Parsis, and Jesuits debate with one another at his court. His administration, with a land survey for taxation and a ranking order of officials, and the buildings of Fatehpur Sikri, shaped India into the British period.
oda-nobunaga-okehazama#title: Oda Nobunaga wins at Okehazama and begins the unification of Japan
oda-nobunaga-okehazama#summary: With a surprise victory over a far superior army, the provincial lord Oda Nobunaga rises to become the leading power in a fragmented Japan.
oda-nobunaga-okehazama#text: Since the Ōnin War of 1467, Japan had been in the Sengoku period, the age of the warring states, broken up into dozens of principalities, while the shogun in Kyoto was powerless. In 1560 Nobunaga attacked the camp of the lord Imagawa Yoshimoto at Okehazama with a few thousand warriors and killed him. In the following years he took Kyoto, in 1575 at Nagashino deployed muskets in great numbers, which Portuguese traders had brought into the country, and broke the power of the Buddhist monasteries. After his death in 1582, Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu completed the unification of the country.
silberflotten-und-manila-galeone#title: Silver fleets and the Manila galleon
silberflotten-und-manila-galeone#summary: Andrés de Urdaneta finds the return route across the Pacific; Spanish fleets now link the Americas with Europe and Asia.
silberflotten-und-manila-galeone#text: To protect itself against pirates and hostile powers, Spain had its ships sail in armed convoys from the middle of the 16th century: every year one fleet sailed to Veracruz and one to Cartagena and Panama, and together they brought silver to Seville. In 1565 the navigator and friar Andrés de Urdaneta discovered a route that led back from the Philippines to Mexico with favourable winds. From then on the Manila galleon linked Acapulco with Manila, where Mexican silver was exchanged for Chinese silk and porcelain. For the first time a trade network arose that spanned all inhabited continents. The galleon sailed until 1815.
idris-alauma-staerkt-bornu#title: Idris Alooma makes Bornu a military power
idris-alauma-staerkt-bornu#summary: The king of Bornu strengthens his realm with firearms, Turkish instructors and Islamic law.
idris-alauma-staerkt-bornu#text: Idris Alooma ruled Kanem-Bornu in the late 16th century; the exact years of his reign are disputed among historians. He obtained muskets and instructors from Ottoman-ruled Tripoli and with them raised a corps of musketeers that gave him military superiority over his neighbors. In numerous campaigns he extended his rule around Lake Chad and also regained the old heartland of Kanem. After a pilgrimage to Mecca he promoted Islamic law, mosques and scholars. His court chronicler Ahmad ibn Furtu described his deeds in detail.
seeschlacht-von-lepanto#summary: The fleet of the Holy League under Don John of Austria defeats the Ottoman fleet in the Gulf of Patras.
seeschlacht-von-lepanto#text: After the Ottomans had attacked Venetian Cyprus in 1570, Spain, Venice and the pope formed the Holy League. On 7 October 1571 more than 400 warships met in the Gulf of Patras; the League's fleet under Don John of Austria won, and the Ottoman admiral Ali Pasha was killed. Among the wounded was the future writer Miguel de Cervantes. Europe celebrated the victory, but the Ottomans rebuilt their fleet within a year and kept Cyprus, which Venice ceded in 1573.
bartholomaeusnacht#title: St. Bartholomew's Day massacre in Paris
bartholomaeusnacht#summary: In the night of 24 August 1572, thousands of Huguenots are murdered in Paris; the massacre becomes a symbol of the wars of religion.
bartholomaeusnacht#text: Numerous Huguenot leaders had come to Paris for the wedding of the Protestant Henry of Navarre to Marguerite de Valois, the king's sister. After a failed attempt on the life of Admiral Coligny, the court, under the influence of the queen mother Catherine de' Medici, had the leaders killed; the mob widened the violence into a massacre that claimed up to 10,000 victims in Paris and the provinces. The pope had a commemorative medal struck; Protestant princes were appalled. The wars of religion ended only in 1598, when Henry IV, by then a Catholic, granted the Huguenots freedom of worship with the Edict of Nantes.
gregorianischer-kalender#summary: Pope Gregory XIII reforms the calendar: 4 October 1582 is followed immediately by 15 October.
gregorianischer-kalender#text: The Julian calendar, in force since Caesar, had fallen ten days behind the solar year, so that Easter moved further and further away from the beginning of spring. A commission around the astronomer Christopher Clavius calculated a new rule for leap years, according to which full centuries are leap years only if they are divisible by 400. Catholic countries adopted the reform at once, the Protestant territories of Germany only in 1700, Great Britain in 1752, and Russia in 1918. Today the Gregorian calendar is the basis of the civil year worldwide.
jermak-beginnt-die-eroberung-sibiriens#t: Yermak begins the conquest of Siberia
jermak-beginnt-die-eroberung-sibiriens#s: The Cossack leader Yermak captures the capital of the Khanate of Sibir and opens Russia's way across northern Asia to the Pacific.
